items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial is testing a new drug called ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd) against standard chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will determine if patients live longer overall and live longer without the cancer growing compared to chemotherapy. This is a major trial testing a novel targeted therapy approach.

items.title: PROLONG Study: Olaparib Combination in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This study will collect real-world data on olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) combined with hormone therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who previously received hormone treatment. The goal is to inform clinical practice and treatment guidelines for PARP inhibitor combinations in diverse populations. The trial has not yet started recruiting.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lu-177-PSMA-617 Phase 1 Dose-Escalation Study
items.summary: This phase 1 study is testing different doses of cabozantinib combined with Lu-177-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is currently suspended but aims to find the safest and most effective dose combination. This represents a novel combination of targeted therapies.

items.title: XL092 Phase 2 Trial for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 2 trial is testing an oral drug called XL092 taken once daily in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Researchers will evaluate how well the drug works after 16 weeks and monitor its safety. Patients will have regular clinic visits for checkups and tests.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lu-177 Vipivotide Tetraxetan Phase 2 Study
items.summary: This phase 2 study compares the combination of luxdegalutamide (an androgen receptor inhibitor) at two different doses plus Lu-177 radioligand therapy versus radioligand therapy alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who received prior hormone therapy and up to two chemotherapy regimens. The goal is to select the best dose for phase 3 trials.

items.title: Pembrolizumab Combination Therapies in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests pembrolizumab (an immunotherapy) combined with various other treatments including olaparib, docetaxel, enzalutamide, abiraterone, and lenvatinib in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial has multiple arms testing different combinations and is no longer recruiting. Results will inform which combinations work best.

items.title: BNT324 Versus Docetaxel Phase 3 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial compares BNT324 (a novel investigational drug) against standard chemotherapy (docetaxel) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with hormone therapy but not chemotherapy. The study will determine if BNT324 helps patients live longer and delays cancer progression better than standard treatment.

items.title: FTT PET/CT Imaging to Detect PARP Activity in Metastatic Prostate
items.summary: This recruiting study will use a new type of PET scan called FTT to look at PARP enzyme activity in cancer sites in up to 30 men with metastatic prostate cancer. Patients will have a baseline scan before starting new treatment and optionally a second scan after treatment begins. Results will be compared with tissue biopsies when available.

items.title: BMS-986365 Versus Investigator's Choice Phase 3 Trial in mCRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial compares BMS-986365 (a novel drug) against the doctor's choice of therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will assess how well BMS-986365 works compared to other available treatments and monitor safety. This represents a potential new treatment option.

items.title: STEAP1 CAR T-Cell Therapy Plus Enzalutamide in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This recruiting phase 1/2 trial tests a cell therapy called STEAP1 CAR T-cells combined with enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. CAR T-cells are immune cells modified to attack cancer cells. The study will determine safety and effectiveness of this immunotherapy approach for an incurable disease.

items.title: Xaluritamig Phase 1 Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 1 trial is determining the safety profile of xaluritamig in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Phase 1 trials test new drugs to find the safest dose and identify side effects before larger studies begin.

items.title: HLD-0915 Phase 1/2 Study in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 1/2 trial is testing the safety and effectiveness of HLD-0915 in patients with metastatic prostate cancer who have progressed after prior treatments. The study will evaluate the drug in various prostate cancer populations to determine its potential benefit.

items.title: Xaluritamig Combined With Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This recruiting phase 1 trial is testing xaluritamig combined with either darolutamide or abiraterone (both hormone therapies) in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The main goal is to evaluate safety and tolerability of these combinations. This targets earlier-stage metastatic disease.

items.title: Lutetium Lu-177 Dotatate for Metastatic Prostate Cancer With Neuroendocrine Features
items.summary: This recruiting phase 2 trial tests lutetium Lu-177 dotatate radioligand therapy in men with metastatic prostate cancer that has neuroendocrine features. This is a specific aggressive subtype of prostate cancer. The radiation drug targets and kills cells that have somatostatin receptors common in neuroendocrine tumors.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Investigator's Choice Phase 3 Trial
items.summary: This recruiting phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig combined with abiraterone against the doctor's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The main goal is to determine if patients receiving the combination live longer overall.

items.title: DNA Vaccines Plus Pembrolizumab in Castration-Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests one or two DNA vaccines (pTVG-HP and pTVG-AR) given with pembrolizumab immunotherapy in men with castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer. The hypothesis is that two vaccines will generate stronger immune responses against the tumor, leading to PSA declines and objective responses. Treatment lasts up to 2 years.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper explains how chronic inflammation drives prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance through NFκB and JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways. These inflammatory signals work together with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor growth, immune evasion, and metastasis. Understanding these pathways may lead to new treatment strategies targeting inflammation in advanced disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study tested a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a protein highly expressed in aggressive prostate cancer) combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. The vaccine generated strong immune responses, eliminated tumors, and prevented lung metastasis in animal models. The approach increased immune system activation and enhanced response to immunotherapy.

items.title: PI3K/AKT Pathway Targeting in Prostate Cancer With PTEN Loss
items.summary: This review discusses targeting the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway in prostate cancer, particularly in tumors with PTEN gene loss. PTEN deficiency is common in advanced prostate cancer and activates this pathway. The paper covers biomarker-guided therapy approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from drugs targeting this pathway.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer With Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict overall survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who did not have surgery. The model found that Gleason score (tumor aggressiveness) was more important than clinical stage for predicting survival. Patients with high Gleason scores, visceral metastases, and advanced age had significantly higher mortality risk.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immunotherapy Effectiveness in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials with 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitors in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. Results showed modest benefits: 63% alive at 1 year, 39% at 2 years. Combination immunotherapy with other agents showed better survival than single-agent immunotherapy, though overall responses remain limited.

items.title: New Biosensor Detects Multiple Prostate Cancer Markers Simultaneously
items.summary: Researchers developed a highly sensitive biosensor using quantum dots that can simultaneously detect PSA and AFP (two cancer markers) in a single test. This technology could enable earlier cancer detection and better monitoring of disease. The approach uses fluorescent nanoparticles linked to antibodies to detect very low levels of these proteins.

items.title: Targeting Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer Immunotherapy
items.summary: This review examines regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the prostate tumor microenvironment and their role in helping cancer evade the immune system. High numbers of Tregs in tumor tissue are associated with more than double the risk of cancer recurrence. The paper discusses current and emerging therapies that target Tregs to improve immunotherapy effectiveness.
